newsitem.title: USA: Somanetics says monitor Phase I research completed.
newsitem.headline: Somanetics says monitor Phase I research completed.

text.p: Somanteics Corp said Monday its research partner, NeuroPhysics Corp, completed the Phase I feasibility research work of a new approach for monitoring fetal cerebral oxygen during birth.

NeuroPhysics submitted a report on the research to the National Institute of Health. Somanetics has certain ownership and commercialization rights, including worldwide rights to market and sell products developed in conjunction with NeuroPhysics, Somanetics said.

"With this demonstration that the underlying physics work, the research now shifts to whether a useful, reliable, simple-to-use, and inexpensive device can be developed that is accepted by practitioners in the clinical setting," said Hugh Stoddart, NeuroPhysics' chairman, said in a news release.

The development of a fetal cerebral oximeter is being pursued to address the need to assess fetal distress during labor and delivery, Somanetics said. NeuroPhysics has been invited by the NIH to submit a Phase II contract, which if awarded, will include the development of a working prototype device and animal model and clinical testing.
Somanetics shares closed up 3/8 at 3-7/8 Monday.
